matched_rules.because: A utility voltage sag occurred and chillers failed to restart, indicating mechanical cooling may be compromised; the rule directs verifying cooling and planning for thermal buffer depletion.
A utility voltage sag tripped multiple chillers offline and manual restarts are required across two data halls; the rule mandates a load-based restart sequence across data halls.
Chillers supporting the data halls have tripped offline; the rule requires confirming the minimum operational chiller count per data hall.
Multiple chillers require manual restart and the Chiller Management System has not been changed to prevent restart failures; the rule advises staging extra technicians.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running and assess thermal buffer status.
Count how many chillers each impacted data hall still has running against its minimum requirement (at least four per hall).
Sequence manual chiller restarts by data hall load so that every impacted data hall gets partial cooling early, rather than finishing one data hall before starting the next.
Increase technician staffing at the datacenter so manual restart procedures can be executed promptly and in parallel across data halls.

escalate.to: facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer
escalate.reason: Mechanical cooling is confirmed shut down (chillers failed to restart) and multiple chillers require manual restart across more than one data hall, triggering escalation conditions for R-001, R-010, and R-012.

not_covered: No rule addresses the specific scenario of a voltage sag causing 13 chillers to fail automatic restart while the site is not on generator power and storms are not mentioned.
No rule covers the coordination of remote resets versus manual restarts when chillers fail to restart automatically after a voltage sag.
No rule addresses the potential need to transfer the datacenter to generator power when only a voltage sag (not a full outage) has occurred and storms are not active.

per_finding.note: Triage names the voltage sag tripping chillers offline across data halls.
Triage does not mention incremental load growth or the CMS timing defect susceptibility.
Triage directs sequencing restarts by load and assessing thermal buffer, but does not name the chilled water loop overheating that blocks the final five chillers.
Triage does not mention the chiller self-protection mechanism inhibiting restart at elevated water temperatures.
Triage does not direct or anticipate the remote shutdown of IT infrastructure to address thermal runaway.
Triage does not state that shutting down IT load would cool the chilled water loop and enable chiller restart.
Triage notes the CMS has not been changed but does not apply the remediation of changing control timing logic.
Triage already directs a load-based restart sequence across data halls to give partial cooling early.
Triage already directs increasing technician staffing to execute manual restarts promptly.
Triage applies load-based sequencing and extra staffing but does not state that staffing alone would have sufficed with that sequence.
Triage directs assessing thermal buffer status, pointing toward thermal-driven IT shutdowns, but does not name the automatic infrastructure shutdown or service impact.
